title: Romance Advice I Wish My Parents Taught Me: the jealousy paragraphs to teach me from
intro: Your two versions taught me a lot, and I used them on the three other stretches with the same problem. Two of them now read Human inside their sections: Romance ("play the damsel ... pretending she can’t open a jar") and Idealization ("she can go from worshipping me to hating me, first in private and then in front of everybody"). My message has the links.

These three jealousy paragraphs are the last ones still flagged. Each of my newest versions reads Human by itself, but together, and inside the section, they read AI, the way S2 did before your version. Press Edit it and write them the way you’d say them; the page shows the section as your live post has it.

teach.label: Teach me
teach.about: paragraphs that read AI in every wording I tried, in their section: how you would say them teaches me how to say the rest

suggestions.whose: he asked: Joel, 2026-11-07 12:08 UTC, in the bad trips lane (gate bad-trips-2026-11-07c makes it every lane's rule): "if you can't figure out how to humanize things, give me the top most important paragraphs (usually 1 or 2) that youu think i could teach you from that would help you humanize the rest, and give me your best tries on those to fix."
suggestions.title: Mentioning attractions, promises of exclusivity, and how polyamory can be dishonest too
suggestions.reading: In the section as your live post has it: [28% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/184babff-d20a-4383-8e5d-c125b55aa48b), AI Low and Medium on all three paragraphs, and his 366 and 370 Low around them.
suggestions.tested:
1. Idioms in place of the abstract words ("a whole sit-down talk", "each other’s one and only forever", "can’t keep it in their pants"): the three with 366 and 370 read [95% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/613a0e10-1633-4eed-8792-1c5e763740fe), worse than the live words.

2. A particular scene in each, your plain words back: 367 "I’d rather be able to say “she’s cute” about a woman at the next table, and have my girlfriend say the same about some guy, without it turning into a fight. If only the serious crushes get mentioned, every mention turns into a confession, so people end up hiding all of them." read [Human, Medium then Low](https://www.pangram.com/history/2a7438bb-34a3-43db-865e-8ea8126efeec) by itself; 368 with 369 read [100% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/5a483771-c3cd-4cdd-89bc-07f2ba9838aa).

3. My best: 369 told as what people do, the way your S2 told the monks’ reasons: "Lots of couples promise forever and nobody else. Look around at how many actually live that way. In a polyamorous relationship the boundaries might be more negotiable, but then somebody has to sit down and negotiate them, down to who gets to stay the night." and "Polyamory can be dishonest too, like when someone who can’t get close to any one person dates four at once and calls it polyamory. Or when someone keeps cheating until they finally announce they’re poly, without necessarily doing the work on themselves that would make it ethical. If you can’t do monogamy, say so, since pretending can do more damage than an affair would have." Together they read [Human, Medium and High](https://www.pangram.com/history/96386c46-ec98-45ad-bd35-41e0f5dddde8), and 369 alone [Human, High](https://www.pangram.com/history/4b7466bb-9691-42f1-ab09-546c3fc28664). With 367 and with 366 and 370 around them, [94.8% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/4d8ad356-99b1-48ed-824d-5d20731b67a8); in the whole section, [26% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/f6838232-0d06-4160-b614-171df927ee32): AI Medium on 367’s second sentence, AI High on 368, AI Low on 369 with 370.

4. The links a fresh reader found missing put in words ("For that to stay honest, I’d rather we could both mention attractions to other people casually, ...", "... so a lot of them end up pretending. Polyamory leaves those rules open, ...", "Or when someone who can’t stop cheating just renames it polyamory, ..."): the section read [31.7% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/8d1b8eb6-deb9-4a95-a0d9-707cb70ac464), worse.
suggestions.why: Every version of mine reads Human by itself and AI once the three sit together, which is what happened to S2 until your version. Your fixes I carried (concrete things in place of lists, a reason with since, what people do in place of what an idea does) fixed Romance and Idealization, and fixed each of these alone, but not the three together. Something about how they follow one another is still mine.
suggestions.sense: A fresh reader read your live three for sense (SENSE-T2.md beside this page) and found the links between them missing: "I would rather" has no alternative and never says to whom; the step from "only the serious ones" to "a major event" isn’t said; 368 jumps from mentioning attractions to promises to polyamory; "negotiable" doesn’t mean "negotiating is required"; 369 answers a claim nobody made, its "too" points at a dishonesty only implied, and "a way to admit a lack of self-control" sits oddly beside "dishonest", since admitting is honest. My fourth try put each link in words and read worse, so I don’t trust my reading of how these three should follow one another.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: write the three the way you’d say them. What they say has to stay: you’d rather any attraction, even a small one, could be mentioned casually, since if only serious ones get mentioned each becomes a big event and people stop saying anything; exclusive lifelong partnership is promised far more often than lived; polyamory’s boundaries are more negotiable, so they have to be negotiated; polyamory isn’t automatically better, since it can be a way to cope with not connecting deeply with one person, or to admit a lack of self-control without the work that would make it ethical; and if you can’t do monogamy, saying so is more honest than pretending, which can do more damage than an outside connection would have.
